summary.text: A 69-year-old Caucasian man presented with an asymptomatic dark-brown to black pigmented macula on the glans and foreskin that had been present for several years and rapidly enlarged in the last few months. Urologists had excised the foreskin and taken glans biopsies for diagnosis before he came to the plastic surgical team.

Histological examination showed melanoma in situ, with numerous atypical melanocytic cells and no dermal invasion of atypical melanocytes. The patient was assessed as having AJCC stage 0 (TiS M0 N0) melanoma of the penis.
The lesion was widely excised with a healthy margin of 1 cm all over except close to the urethral meatus. A full thickness mucosal graft from the oral cavity repaired the glans defect.

At the sixth clinical follow-up the patient was alive and disease free at 50 months after surgery, with no recurrence or metastasis, no functional disorders, and no lower urinary tract symptoms or erectile dysfunction observed.
